This is the section an executive quotes in a meeting, and it only works if every line is real.> | Who | When | What they said | Where | |---|---|---|---| | | | "" | | ## What the site does well <2–4 bullets. A report that cannot say anything positive is as untrustworthy as one that cannot say anything negative.> ## Against comparable sites ## What each check looked for | Check | Question it answers | |---|---| | **Clarity** | Can a visitor say what this is, who it is for, and what to do next? | | **Ideal Customer Profiles** | Who should this product be built and sold for, on the evidence of what it is? | ## How each area scores ## How to read these findings | Severity | Meaning | |---|---| | 🔴 **P0** | Blocks the job, or breaks trust badly enough that people leave | | 🟠 **P1** | They get through, but would not become a customer | | 🟡 **P2** | Noticeable friction; erodes value over time | | ⚪ **P3** | Polish. Worth fixing, changes nothing on its own | ## Raised by more than one check ## Limits of this assessment - ``` #### ⚑ Sections this document must NOT contain - **No verdict sentence at the top.** The document opens with a description of the thing assessed. A reader who has never seen the product cannot use a verdict about it. The verdict opens the Top 5 instead, where the evidence for it is directly underneath. *(Gate check 6 applies to lens summaries only.)* - **No "Recommended first action".** The Top 5 is ranked, so its first row is already the recommended first action. Repeating it invites the two to drift. - **No "technical facts worth separating out".** Anything technical belongs to the Technical check, where a reader looking for it will go. A summary that keeps its own technical annexe is two reports. - **No section numbers written by hand.** `render_report.py` numbers every section in document order, so an inserted section cannot leave the index pointing at the wrong place. - **No severity tally of your own.** The cover already carries the finding count and the P0/P1/P2/P3 split. A second copy in the body is how the two come to disagree. - **No invented or improved quotation.** "In their own words" carries the persona's exact text with a source. # Nimbus Notes — Website assessment — 8 September 2026

## What this is

- Nimbus Notes is a notes app that keeps notes on the device first and syncs them between devices. It sells to individuals and teams through three plans: Starter, Team and Enterprise.
- Nimbus Notes Ltd has eight people. Priya Raman founded it in 2023, it is based in Bristol, UK (company number 14482201), and it stores data in Frankfurt by default.
- No plan shows a price. Every plan says "Contact sales".

## How it was produced

- Two stand-in visitors, each with their own goal, used the real marketing site in a browser and everything they did was recorded. One was on a desktop at 1440×900 for 6 min 30 s. The other was on an iPhone 13 for 2 min 50 s.
- A separate reviewer then scored that recording for one thing: whether a first-time visitor can tell what the product is. The reviewer saw the recording only, not the visitors' goals in advance.
- Both visitors were made up for this test from generic buyer types. Neither is a real customer.

## Contents

## Objectives

## Top 5 — fix these first

Neither visitor could find out from the site what Nimbus Notes is or who it is for, and the one button that offers to show the product does nothing.

| # | Severity | What is happening | What it costs | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | P1 | The top of the home page says "Your thoughts, everywhere." over an abstract purple image. Nothing in view says what the product is. | Both visitors guessed "notes app" from the name alone. Neither ever got to a point where they actually understood it. A visitor who does not already know the name leaves with a guess. | Copy change |
| 2 | P1 | The only button in the hero, "See it in action", links to nowhere (`href="#"`). Clicking or tapping it does nothing. | Both visitors tried it and left without ever seeing the product. The sceptical visitor stopped 20 seconds after tapping it. | Build |

- Only two findings were serious enough for this list. The other six are moderate or cosmetic, so they are left out rather than used to pad it to five.
- Row 1 is a copy change: one plain sentence in the hero. Row 2 needs something real to link to, such as a screenshot, a short video or a tour section.

## What a buyer could and could not establish

| Question the buyer had | Answer from the site |
|---|---|
| What is this? | **No, only a guess.** "Notes app" came from the name at 00:06 (desktop) and 00:08 (phone). The headline never says. |
| Who is it for? | **Not on the home page.** "For individuals." / "For growing teams." appears only on the Pricing cards, one click away. |
| What does it cost? | **No.** The desktop visitor looked from 01:48 to 02:30 across Pricing and the demo form. All three plans say "Contact sales". The only explanation is "workspace type and sync topology". |
| What does it actually do? | **Eventually, on About.** Works offline, exports to Markdown, data in Frankfurt. The desktop visitor got there at 04:20, after four pages and a 404 on Features. |
| Who is behind it? | **Yes, on About.** Named founder, address and company number. Phone visitor at 01:30, desktop visitor at 03:50. |
| Where is my data stored? | **Yes, but on About, not Privacy.** "In the EU (Frankfurt) by default", reached by the phone visitor at 01:50. |
| Who is my data shared with? | **No.** The Privacy page says "partners and service providers" and never names them. |

## In their own words

| Who | When | What they said | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| evaluator | 00:06 | "What do I think this is? Some kind of notes app, from the name. The headline doesn't say." | `persona-evaluator/session.log:6` · Top 5 row 1 |
| sceptic | 00:08 | "What is it? Notes, I think. For who? Doesn't say." | `persona-sceptic/session.log:6` · Top 5 row 1 |
| evaluator | 00:18 | "\"bi-directional sync graph with a zero-knowledge vault\" — I don't know what either of those means. I'll assume it syncs." | `persona-evaluator/session.log:10` |
| evaluator | 00:40 | "Clicked \"See it in action\". Nothing happened. The page didn't move. Clicked again. Still nothing." | `persona-evaluator/session.log:12` · Top 5 row 2 |
| sceptic | 02:20 | "I want to see it \"remember\" something. The button does nothing when I tap it." | `persona-sceptic/session.log:13` · Top 5 row 2 |
| evaluator | 02:10 | "I don't know what my workspace type is. I haven't got one." | `persona-evaluator/session.log:18` · `02-pricing.png` |
| evaluator | 03:50 | "That's the first thing on this site that felt like a real business." | `persona-evaluator/session.log:24` · `05-about.png` |
| evaluator | 04:20 | "Those are actual answers. Why isn't this on the home page?" | `persona-evaluator/session.log:25` · `05-about.png` |
| sceptic | 01:30 | "Priya Raman, Bristol, 2023, company number 14482201, eight people. Good. That is a real company." | `persona-sceptic/session.log:11` · `02-about.png` |
| sceptic | debrief Q6 | "\"It remembers everything.\" No — nothing on the site shows it remembering anything; the button that might have doesn't work." | `persona-sceptic/persona-debrief.md` Q6 · Top 5 row 2 |

- The speakers are personas built for this test from generic buyer types. They are not customers.

## What the site does well

- The About page answers the questions a careful buyer asks: works offline, exports to Markdown on every plan, data in Frankfurt by default. Both visitors called these real answers.
- The site says plainly who is behind it: a named founder, a street address in Bristol and a company number. That was the first point at which both visitors believed it was a real business.
- The Pricing cards say who each plan is for in plain words: "For individuals." / "For growing teams." That line works. It just sits on the wrong page.

## What each check looked for

| Check | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| **Clarity** | Can a visitor say what this is, who it is for, and what to do next? |

## How each area scores

## How to read these findings

| Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 🔴 **P0** | Blocks the job, or breaks trust badly enough that people leave |
| 🟠 **P1** | They get through, but would not become a customer |
| 🟡 **P2** | Noticeable friction; erodes value over time |
| ⚪ **P3** | Polish. Worth fixing, changes nothing on its own |

- Only one check was scored, so no finding here is backed by a second, independent check. Both findings in the Top 5 were seen by both visitors on separate devices.
- The full findings, with screenshots, log lines and steps to reproduce, are in `clarity/findings-final.md`.

## Limits of this assessment

- **Visitors were constructed, not recruited.** Both are generic personas, and their sessions are a hand-written test fixture, not a live browser run. Treat the quotes as illustrations of the problems, not as customer research.
- **Only clarity was scored.** The run also planned conversion, trust, technical, SEO and AEO checks. Evidence was captured for those but they were not scored. The price, demo-form, privacy and cookie-bar problems the visitors ran into are therefore not ranked here.
- **The objective was not scored either.** No `objectives/results.md` existed when this was written, so this summary says nothing on whether a visitor can find a price without giving an email.
- **Parts of the site were never seen.** `/features.html` returned a 404. The desktop below-the-fold screenshot (`01-scrolled.png`) came out blank, so those sections are read from the log and page markup only. The phone visitor never opened Pricing.
- **Short visits on two devices.** One desktop and one iPhone, at standard depth, 6 min 30 s and 2 min 50 s. No tablet, no signed-in product, no competitor comparison.
